messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing ~30s window in eu-west canary where SSE connections close with no error, client reconnects but gets no resume token. Console still shows session as ACTIVE :thinking_face
aj: repro steps? is this tied to quota or routing?
kevin: saw similar in staging yesterday. Proxy sent a 200 then closed socket, no final event. client logs: ```EventSource error: closing socket without EOF```
lisa: console heartbeat shows last_seen 2s before close, then node-level metric for socket_close spikes. No quota messages.
maria: tagged example trace ids: trace:eu-42/9a7b; route: r-v2. Can we add telemetry to mark 'silent_close' vs 'normal_close' so console can surface it?
kevin: agree. Also need to know whether it was our edge (nginx/proxy) or upstream runtime. Current route mapping doesn't persist proxy instance in trace.
aj: quick workaround: add fallback policy that forces websocket fallback for affected routes in canary. But that's heavy-handed.
lisa: +1 for telemetry first. If we can attach probe that records tcp FIN vs RST vs HTTP 1.1 chunk end, we can classify.
infra-bot: deploy started: canary/edge-proxy v2.3.1 -> 3 nodes (initiated by @deploy-bot)
kevin: for instrumentation I'd add two tags: `connection_termination=socket|application` and `termination_cause=silence|eof|reset`. Then console can alert when termination_cause==silence.
maria: also we need to decide UX: when console shows ACTIVE but client lost resume token, it creates confusion. Maybe show a soft-warning: "client-side reconnects observed" and link to traces.
aj: question: are we sure resume token was not persisted to KV? Could be race where token write lagged and client reconnects before it's durable. Any k/v write failures?
lisa: looked at kv write logs around those traces — write latencies ~120ms but success. Not seeing obvious errors.
kevin: could still be race if client reconnects faster than write ack propagated to the proxy that handles resume. How about changing client reconnect jitter to >= 200ms for canary to reduce likelihood?
maria: let's not alter client behavior in prod. prefer server-side: hold connection for extra 250ms of grace after sending final chunk to allow token flush.
aj: that seems reasonable. Implementation path: 1) add termination tagging telemetry (kevin), 2) console UI flag for silent_close (lisa + console team), 3) add 250ms grace on proxy close (eng-platform rollout), 4) canary with 10% traffic.
kevin: PR in progress for telemetry: will emit `termination_cause` and include `proxy_instance` id. ETA today EOD.
lisa: I'll add a console panel card mapping termination types to counts and a drilldown to traces. Also add alert for >1% silent_close in 5m.
maria: can we also emit a rate-limited note to the client header so SDKs can surface a different reconnect path? e.g., `X-Resume-Hint: pending`
aj: maybe. But I'd rather keep it internal until we confirm.
infra-bot: deploy success: canary/edge-proxy v2.3.1 -> rolled to 3 nodes (0 failures)
kevin: added log lines `termination_cause=silence proxy_instance=eu-edge-7` to traces for the test traces.
maria: observed two repros after telemetry patch but still silent. Lisa, console card looks good — pulled up traces. Root cause looks like proxy sends an HTTP-level keepalive termination when backend returns `connection: close` without final chunk.
lisa: will add a console note that flags routes with backend `connection: close` header + silent_close spikes.
aj: plan approved. Rollout steps posted to the playbook in #eng-oncall. cc @deploy-bot
deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled in 10m, will monitor metrics and auto-rollback on error rate >0.5%
kevin: follow-up task: add unit test to simulate backend closing without final chunk and ensure proxy grace works.
maria: thanks team. tagging this thread for postmortem if it reaches >0.5% in prod. :thumbsup:
